name: Alport syndrome - sensorineural hearing loss features

clinicalPearls: A type IV collagen disorder combining progressive hereditary nephritis, sensorineural hearing loss and characteristic ocular changes
Hearing loss is bilateral, high-frequency and progressive, typically emerging in later childhood or adolescence rather than at birth
Most cases are X-linked from COL4A5 mutations, so affected males are usually more severely affected than female carriers; autosomal recessive and dominant forms involve COL4A3 and COL4A4
Renal disease presents with haematuria progressing to proteinuria and declining renal function, and is the dominant determinant of prognosis
Ocular signs such as anterior lenticonus and retinal flecks are highly suggestive when present
The hearing loss reflects abnormal type IV collagen in the cochlear basement membranes rather than a structural malformation
Persistent haematuria with a family history and hearing loss should prompt evaluation for Alport syndrome
reference.pathophysiology: Alport syndrome is caused by mutations in the genes encoding the alpha-3, alpha-4 and alpha-5 chains of type IV collagen, a key component of specialised basement membranes. In the kidney, defective collagen disrupts the glomerular basement membrane, producing progressive nephritis with haematuria and eventual renal failure. The same collagen is present in basement membranes of the cochlea, and its abnormality is thought to impair the mechanical and metabolic environment of the organ of Corti, causing progressive high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss. Defective basement-membrane collagen in the lens capsule and retina underlies the associated ocular abnormalities.
additionalDifferentials: Thin basement membrane nephropathy (benign familial haematuria)
Other causes of progressive sensorineural hearing loss in adolescence
IgA nephropathy and other glomerulonephritides with haematuria
Other syndromic hearing loss with systemic involvement
Acquired hearing loss from noise or ototoxic exposure
Fabry disease and other inherited disorders with renal and sensory features
additionalInvestigations: Serial audiometry to document progressive high-frequency sensorineural loss
Urinalysis for haematuria and proteinuria with renal function testing
Ophthalmic examination for lenticonus and retinal flecks
Renal biopsy with electron microscopy of the glomerular basement membrane where diagnosis is unclear
Molecular genetic testing of type IV collagen genes with family screening
redFlags: Rising proteinuria or declining renal function indicating progression toward renal failure
Rapidly progressive hearing loss affecting communication
Visual disturbance suggesting lenticonus or retinal involvement
Family history of renal failure and deafness indicating inherited disease
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is dominated by the renal disease, which in more severe (often X-linked male) cases progresses to end-stage renal failure requiring dialysis or transplantation; the sensorineural hearing loss is progressive but manageable with amplification, and does not itself threaten life.
pitfalls: Attributing isolated haematuria to a benign cause and missing evolving Alport syndrome
Assuming congenital deafness, when Alport hearing loss develops progressively later
Overlooking female carriers who may have milder or later renal and hearing involvement
Neglecting regular renal monitoring while focusing on the hearing loss
references: Cummings Otolaryngology: Head and Neck Surgery
